# `js/todo-marker`

**JavaScript and TypeScript TODO comments carry a ticket and, when asked, a date**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/markers` at `error` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (a ticket and a date are facts about the work that only the author knows; the engine can't invent them) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |

## What it checks

A comment line that opens with a marker tag (`TODO`, `FIXME`, `HACK` by default) in a `//` or `/* … */` comment carries a ticket, and a date when the project asks for one: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): text`. The ticket and the date go in the parentheses, in either order, either one optional unless required; any other item in them (an owner's name) is ignored. The tag must start the comment line, so a sentence that merely mentions a TODO is not a marker.

A date that is written is always enforced, whether or not `require_date` is set: it is **expired** from the as-of date on (`--as-of`, `CODELAW_AS_OF`, else `HEAD`'s commit date, never the clock: [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md) decision 9) and is a **warning** for the `warn_days` before it. A date that is not a calendar day is reported too. With no as-of date, only the missing and the malformed are reported.

**Why:** A TODO with no ticket has no owner and no place to be tracked, and one with no date never comes due; both outlive the people who wrote them. Naming a ticket ties the comment to the work, and a date makes the comment fail loudly the day it is overdue instead of rotting quietly.

**Configuration** is the `[todo]` table of `codelaw.toml` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md) decision 11a), one for every language:

```toml
[todo]
tags           = ["TODO", "FIXME", "HACK"]   # the words that open a marker
require_ticket = true                         # a ticket is required (default)
require_date   = false                        # a date is required (default: only a written date is enforced)
ticket_pattern = "[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\\d+"        # a whole ticket must match this regular expression
warn_days      = 14                           # warn this many days before the date
```

**A repo full of bare TODOs** gets every one of them at once. Take them into the baseline (`codelaw baseline`) and pay them down, or set `require_ticket = false` and let the rule enforce only the dates that are written.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/markers` sets it to `error`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/markers"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/todo-marker" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/todo-marker" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/todo-marker" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/todo-marker" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/todo-marker" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/todo-marker": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/todo-marker: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/todo-marker expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/todo-marker --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/todo-marker       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/todo-marker  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>  # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Open or find the ticket for the work and write it in the parentheses: `TODO(ABC-123): …`.
2. When the project asks for a date (`require_date`), or the work has a deadline, add it: `TODO(ABC-123, 2027-01-31): …`.
3. For an expired marker: do the work and delete the comment; or, if the work really moves, change the date and say why in the text.
4. If the comment is not a to-do, rewrite it so it does not open with the tag.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
// TODO: handle the empty cart
function total(cart) {
  return cart.items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0);
}
```

#### Do

```js
// TODO(SHOP-214): handle the empty cart
function total(cart) {
  return cart.items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0);
}
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
// FIXME: the badge flickers
const Badge = () => <span>new</span>;
```

#### Do

```jsx
// FIXME(UI-87): the badge flickers
const Badge = () => <span>new</span>;
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
/* HACK: widen until the API is typed */
export const load = (id: string): any => fetch(id);
```

#### Do

```ts
/* HACK(API-9): widen until the API is typed */
export const load = (id: string): any => fetch(id);
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
// TODO: use the design-system button
export const Save = () => <button>Save</button>;
```

#### Do

```tsx
// TODO(UI-31): use the design-system button
export const Save = () => <button>Save</button>;
```
